title: Historical Italian Hours Clock
intro: Italian hours count equal elapsed hours from the most recently computed sunset, rather than from midnight.
structure: The display begins at 00:00 IT at sunset and counts ordinary hours and minutes, with optional seconds. At the next computed sunset it resets to zero. The interval between sunsets varies, so the hour count is not clamped to 23.
example: If sunset was at 18:30, 21:00 is 02:30 IT. At 06:30 the following morning the reading is 12:00 IT, provided no later sunset has occurred.
history: Sunset-origin Italian hours were historically used in parts of Europe. Some historical conventions and instruments expressed the boundary differently; this resource implements zero-based elapsed time.
model: The provider computes sunset candidates using compact solar equation-of-time and declination terms, latitude, east-positive longitude and a 0.833-degree horizon correction. Select the most recent valid sunset in a bounded search, floor elapsed seconds and format ordinary time fields. The next visible boundary is the earlier of the next elapsed-unit boundary or next sunset, rounded upward to milliseconds.
limits: Requires valid latitude and longitude. Missing solar crossings produce N/A; invalid input fails. The solar event is approximate, not an independently observed historical sunset. Civil timezone and daylight saving do not change it.
